review.note: Original OathSteps explanations written against the research report (checked 5 October 2026) and linked official pages. Educational guidance only; an applicant's own USCIS notices and current official instructions govern their case. Not legal advice and no qualified legal or content review has been recorded yet.

stages.title: Explore and prepare
stages.summary: Understand the process and the test that applies to you before you file or while you wait.

items.text: Read the official eligibility information for naturalization and note any question you want to ask a qualified helper.
items.why: OathSteps does not decide eligibility. Official pages and qualified legal help do.

items.text: Locate your N-400 filing date (or note that you have not filed yet) and confirm the civics test version that applies.
items.why: The filing date, not the interview date, selects the 2008 or 2025 test. Filed before 20 October 2025 means the 2008 test; on or after means the 2025 test.

items.text: Review the official information about English exceptions (50/20, 55/15), the 65/20 special consideration and medical disability exceptions (Form N-648) to see if any may apply at filing.
items.why: These routes change what you must study. The app explains them and links to the source; it cannot certify that one applies to you.

items.text: Choose a realistic study routine (even 10 minutes a day) and an optional study deadline.
items.why: Short, regular recall practice beats cramming. A deadline you set is a study goal, not an appointment.

stages.title: Prepare and file Form N-400
stages.summary: Find the official filing instructions and keep your filing date.

items.text: Read the current Form N-400 instructions on uscis.gov and follow them for your situation.
items.why: Forms, fees and filing locations change. The official instructions are the authority.

items.text: After filing, record your filing date in OathSteps so the correct civics test is selected.
items.why: This date is used only to pick the question bank and to count down to your own study goals.

items.text: Start learning the vocabulary used in your own application so you can answer truthfully about it in the interview.
items.why: The officer asks about your N-400. The app helps you practice words and phrases, never invents answers for you.

stages.title: Receipt and biometrics
stages.summary: Understand your receipt notice and any biometrics appointment or reuse notice.

items.text: Read your receipt notice (Form I-797C) and note the receipt date and any instructions.
items.why: Your notices are the record of your case. OathSteps stores only what you type in.

items.text: If you receive a biometrics appointment notice, record the date and follow its instructions. If USCIS reuses earlier biometrics, record that instead.
items.why: Both outcomes are normal. The journey tracker supports an attended appointment or a reuse notice.

sources.label: USCIS: Preparing for your biometric services appointment

stages.title: Interview preparation
stages.summary: Daily recall practice, English tasks and your interview notice.

items.text: Recall civics answers aloud before looking at the answer, and revisit weak questions after a delay.
items.why: The civics test is oral. Recognizing an answer in a list is not the same as saying it.

sources.label: USCIS: The naturalization interview and test

items.text: Practice the mock test in your applicable format and inspect every missed answer.
items.why: 2008 test: up to 10 questions, 6 correct to pass. 2025 test: up to 20 questions, 12 correct to pass, stopping at 12 correct or 9 incorrect. 65/20: 10 of the 20 marked questions, 6 correct to pass.

items.text: Practice reading one sentence aloud, writing one dictated sentence, and understanding interview instructions, unless an English exception applies to you.
items.why: Reading and writing each require one correct sentence out of up to three tries. Speaking is assessed throughout the interview.

items.text: Confirm the answers that depend on current officeholders or your state and district, and record them with the date you checked.
items.why: USCIS expects the official serving at the time of your interview. The app never guesses these; you confirm them from an official source.

items.text: When your interview notice arrives, read it carefully and confirm the time, location and the documents it asks you to bring.
items.why: The notice is the only authoritative document list for your case. OathSteps does not invent one.

sources.label: USCIS: The naturalization interview and test

items.text: Plan transportation, arrival time, and any accessibility or interpreter arrangements your notice allows.
items.why: Practical preparation reduces interview-day stress.

stages.title: Interview outcome
stages.summary: Record what happened and follow the next notice.

items.text: Record the interview outcome you were given: passed, continued, retest scheduled, evidence requested, or another result.
items.why: Different outcomes lead to different next steps. The app keeps approval and oath completion separate.

items.text: If you did not pass a portion of the test, you are generally given a second opportunity for that portion 60 to 90 days later. Follow the notice's dates and keep practicing the failed portion.
items.why: A retest is a normal part of the process, not the end of it.

items.text: If USCIS requests more evidence, follow the request's instructions and deadline exactly.
items.why: Deadlines in a request are set by USCIS, not by the app.

sources.label: USCIS: Responding to a request for evidence

stages.title: Decision and oath
stages.summary: Review the oath notice and complete the ceremony.

items.text: Read your Form N-445 oath ceremony notice, answer its questions truthfully, and bring what it lists.
items.why: You become a citizen when you take the oath, not when the application is approved.

items.text: If you cannot attend, follow the notice's instructions for rescheduling and record the new date when it arrives.
items.why: Rescheduling is supported in the journey tracker; the new date comes from USCIS.

items.text: Apply for a U.S. passport and update your records (for example Social Security) using official guidance.
items.why: These are common next steps after the oath.

items.text: Register to vote if you wish.
items.why: Voting is one of the responsibilities reserved for citizens.

items.text: Review your OathSteps data in Settings: export it, or delete it if you no longer need it.
items.why: Your study history belongs to you.
